# 04 · Practice — Advanced Combinatorics

Order matters. `Foundation` entries isolate a tool; later entries intentionally
mix modelling and algebra. Hints stop before implementation details.

## 1. AtCoder ABC 172 E — NEQ (`Foundation`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc172/tasks/abc172_e) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc172/editorial/52) · English/Japanese
- Train: inclusion--exclusion over equal positions; falling factorials.
- Prerequisite: factorial combinations.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — recognition</summary>Choose both injective sequences, then forbid equality at each aligned position.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2 — reduction</summary>Fix the set of positions forced equal and contract each such pair.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3 — algorithm</summary>Sum by the number of contracted positions, with alternating signs.</details>

## 2. Codeforces 932E — Team Work (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/932/E) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/57796) · English/Russian
- Train: expanding powers in the falling-factorial basis using Stirling numbers.
- Prerequisite: Stirling second kind, binomial identities.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Replace $k^{K}$ by a sum of falling factorials.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Use $k^{\underline j}{N\choose k}=N^{\underline j}{N-j\choose k-j}$.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>The remaining binomial sum is a power of two.</details>

## 3. Codeforces 559C — Gerald and Giant Chess (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/559/C) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/19366) · English/Russian
- Train: poset-style IE / subtracting paths through earlier forbidden points.
- Prerequisite: lattice-path binomials.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Sort forbidden points in a topological order.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Count all paths to a point, then subtract paths whose first bad point was earlier.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>This is triangular DP with a binomial transition.</details>

## 4. AtCoder AGC 005 F — Many Easy Problems (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/agc005/tasks/agc005_f) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/agc005/editorial) · Japanese (browser translation useful)
- Train: tree counting transformed into one factorial-scaled convolution.
- Prerequisite: binomial transform, NTT.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>For each edge, count vertex subsets lying on both sides.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Rearrange the sum so the requested subset size is the outer index.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Reverse one factorial-scaled array to expose convolution.</details>

## 5. Codeforces 995F — Cowmpany Cowmpensation (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/995/F) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/60217) · English/Russian
- Train: polynomial-valued tree DP and interpolation.
- Prerequisite: counting order-preserving labelings; interpolation.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Let a subtree DP depend on the maximum permitted label.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>The DP is a polynomial of bounded degree; children multiply and the parent takes a prefix sum.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Evaluate enough consecutive points, then interpolate at the huge argument.</details>
